candidates.title: Criteria for the economic viability of fusion power plants (Whyte et al., 2026)
candidates.notes: Provides quantitative utilization factor model U = τ_op/(τ_op + τ_rep) applicable to all fusion concepts including IFE. Section 2.8 discusses IFE with flowing liquid wall as a use case. Framework mathematically couples availability/degradation to economic viability. No IFE-specific capacity factor values — requires concept-specific parameterization. Accessible HTML on arxiv.

candidates.title: OSIRIS and SOMBRERO Inertial Fusion Power Plant Designs, Volume 1: Executive Summary & Overview (1992)
candidates.notes: 1992 DOE design study for SOMBRERO (KrF laser IFE) and OSIRIS (heavy-ion IFE) power plants. Designs explicitly assessed for 'reliability and availability, economics, and technology development needs.' SOMBRERO is direct-line ancestor of Xcimer's KrF approach. Likely contains specific availability assumptions for a laser IFE plant. Full PDF accessible via OSTI purl.

candidates.title: OSIRIS and SOMBRERO IFE Power Plant Designs, Volume 2: Designs, Assessments, and Comparisons
candidates.notes: Vol. 2 of the same study — contains the detailed design assessments and comparisons including reliability/availability. PDF too large for WebFetch triage. Purl URL would be https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/836548 — extraction budget exhausted after extracting Vol. 1 and arxiv paper.

candidates.title: Factors influencing the commercialization of inertial fusion energy (PMC7741007)
candidates.notes: Discusses RAMI (reliability, availability, maintainability, inspectability) qualitatively as a cost factor but contains no quantitative availability model or capacity factor values. High-level review paper.

candidates.title: Criteria for the economic viability of fusion power plants — HTML version
candidates.notes: Confirmed accessible HTML version of arxiv preprint. Used for triage only.

candidates.title: IFE-STAR Funding Opportunity Announcement (DOE, 2023)
candidates.notes: FOA document mentions capacity factor qualitatively ('high operating capacity factor' as a goal) but contains no quantitative availability requirements or models. Binary PDF not readable via WebFetch.

candidates.title: Integrated Design of a Robust System for Inertial Fusion Energy (OSTI 1841839)
candidates.notes: Abstract mentions 'high operating capacity factor' as a goal of integrated IFE design. Full PDF compressed and unreadable via WebFetch. Could not confirm quantitative content. Extraction budget exhausted.

candidates.notes: Describes LLNL GEM Excel tool for IFE LCOE estimation. Tool itself covers economics but the ANS article does not contain availability/capacity factor models — just announces the tool's availability.

gaps_attempted.notes: Extracted two sources that address the gap from different angles: (1) Whyte et al. 2026 arxiv preprint provides a mathematical utilization/availability framework that applies to IFE concepts; (2) OSIRIS/SOMBRERO Vol. 1 (1992) is a full IFE plant design study that explicitly covers reliability and availability economics for a KrF laser plant (SOMBRERO) — likely contains the closest available analog to a rep-rate-coupled availability baseline. Highest-relevance inaccessible candidate: Springer paper 'Complexity and Availability for Fusion Power Plants: The Potential Advantages of Inertial Fusion Energy' (paywalled). Candidate for future iteration: OSTI 836548 (OSIRIS/SOMBRERO Vol. 2 — detailed designs and assessments) and OSTI 1841839 (Integrated Design for Robust IFE).
